purpose: Sodium picosulfate is used to treat constipation or to clean out your bowel before a colonoscopy or surgery. It helps get your bowels moving when you are having difficulty going to the toilet. It is also used as part of bowel preparation kits to make sure your colon is completely empty before a medical procedure.
how_it_works: When you swallow sodium picosulfate, bacteria in your gut convert it into an active form that stimulates the muscles in your large intestine to squeeze and move stool along. It also draws water into your bowel, which softens the stool and makes it easier to pass. This combination of muscle stimulation and water retention helps produce a bowel movement, usually within 6 to 12 hours.
common_side_effects: Stomach cramps or discomfort, feeling bloated, diarrhea, nausea, and feeling dehydrated or thirsty. You may also notice some urgency — meaning you might need to get to the bathroom quickly.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you have a blocked bowel, severe dehydration, or certain heart or kidney conditions without first talking to your doctor. Make sure you drink plenty of fluids while taking this medication to avoid dehydration. Do not use it for more than a few days without medical advice, as overuse of laxatives can cause your bowel to become dependent on them. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with it.
typical_dosing: For constipation in adults, the usual dose is 5 to 10 mg taken at bedtime, as a tablet or liquid. For bowel preparation before a procedure, your doctor will give you specific instructions — often two separate doses taken the day before and the morning of your procedure. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions exactly.
